newsitem.title: INDIA: Relatives of hostages arrive in India.
newsitem.headline: Relatives of hostages arrive in India.

text.p: Relatives of two of the four Westerners kidnapped two years ago in India's troubled Jammu and Kashmir state arrived in India on Saturday to appeal for help in finding their loved ones.
Julie Mangan, wife of British kidnap victim Keith Mangan, told reporters after arriving in New Delhi that she had heard different stories, some saying the men had been killed.
"So I came to find out whether these stories are true or not," Julie Mangan said. "I don't believe it myself."

Britons Keith Mangan and Paul Wells, Americans Donald Hutchings and John Childs, German Dirk Hasert and Norwegian Hans Christian Ostroe Mangan, were abducted by Al-Faran guerrillas in July 1995 while trekking in Kashmir.
Childs escaped but Ostroe was later found beheaded. There has been no trace of the other four Westerners, raising doubts about whether they are still alive.

Birgit Hasert, sister of Dirk Hasert, also arrived in New Delhi on Saturday. Hutchings' wife, Jane Schelly, was expected to arrive in India later on Saturday to appeal for help seeking the men, diplomats said.
A pro-government militiaman and a Kashmiri newspaper said earlier this month that the four tourists were shot early in 1996 and buried in a cave.
But Kashmir's chief minister Farooq Abdullah has said authorities have not confirmed this.
"I would like to have the help of the Indian prime minister...to search the area properly because we don't want to be tortured anymore," Julie Mangan said.
Diplomats said the hostages' relatives were likely to visit Kashmir later this month.
